_comment: PROPOSED production configuration for the backup producer — NOT ACTIVATED.
Copy to ~/.config/eanhl/backup.json (mode 600) and review every value before use.
Nothing in this repository reads this file automatically; --config is always explicit.
There are no defaults: every key below is required, and a missing key is a hard error.
backingVolume must be present on BOTH staging and destination. Use null only when the
directory's own filesystem reports the truth. On WSL that is FALSE for anything on the
ext4 root: `df /` reported 945 GB free while the NTFS volume backing that VHDX had 21 GB.
PENDING: `age` is not installed on either host and no keypair exists.
Installing age, generating the keypair and placing the PUBLIC recipient file
are Phase 2 steps requiring explicit operator authorization.
root is on the ext4 WSL root, which lives inside a sparse VHDX on C:.
minFreeBytes guards the ext4 filesystem; backingVolume guards C: itself.
maxPlaintextBytes / maxStagingBytes are hard ceilings, not size predictions:
the observed ~27 MB custom-format dump of a 466 MB database is today's number,
not a guarantee. Raise them deliberately, together with the free-space floors.
maxCiphertextBytes: 5368709120 (5 GiB) is an ALIGNED, EXPLICITLY NON-PRODUCTION
example, chosen to equal maxStagingBytes and the acceptor's example
acceptance.maxCiphertextBytes below (ops/backup/eanhl-backup-accept.example.json).
maxCiphertextBytes == maxStagingBytes here preserves this producer's pre-E3C2
effective ciphertext envelope and E1D's conservative example arithmetic — it grants
the ciphertext no more room than the aggregate staging ceiling already implied, but
it is NOT the least-exposure default; it is not the smallest possible producer
exposure. The least-exposure relationship is acceptance.maxCiphertextBytes ==
staging.maxCiphertextBytes: matching the acceptor's cap means nothing this producer
could publish is one the acceptor would refuse on size alone.
This is NOT an approved production ceiling — see docs/planning/
proton-drive-transport-feasibility.md U5 for what remains open.
/mnt/k is drvfs over NTFS on a separate 8 TB disk. df on a drvfs mount reports the
real NTFS free space, so backingVolume is null here. Rename atomicity, fsync
semantics and Unix modes are NOT assertable on this mount — see the ops doc.
A stale lock is NEVER reclaimed automatically — see the ops doc §2.6. The compensating
control is operationTimeoutMs: no single boundary operation may run longer than this,
so a hung dump or encryptor cannot hold the lock indefinitely.
operationTimeoutMs must exceed the slowest legitimate dump by a wide margin: at ~27 MB
today a dump takes seconds, but this is a ceiling on pathology, not a performance target.
containerProbeTimeoutMs bounds the read-only `ps` probe that decides whether a cancelled
container-side command has ended. If it cannot answer, the lock is RETAINED and an operator
must clear it — uncertainty is never resolved in favour of availability.
